'''''Primula malacoides''''', called the '''fairy primrose''' or '''baby primrose''', is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] species of ''[[Primula]]'' native to the Himalayas, Assam in India, Myanmar, and south-central and south east China.<ref name="702241-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:702241-1 |title=''Primula malacoides'' Franch. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=5 October 2020 }}</ref> It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name=RHSMarch2020>{{cite web |title=''Primula malacoides'' (Mo) fairy primrose |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/13805/Primula-malacoides-(Mo)/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |accessdate=5 October 2020 |quote= }}</ref>

== Description ==
This plant usually has purple flowers, although some may have red, white or bright-pink flowers.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Plants & Flowers » Primula malacoides|url=https://www.plantsrescue.com/tag/primula-malacoides/|access-date=2020-10-24}}</ref>

Their hairy leaves measure at 4–8cm and are a pale-green colour. They usually grow to 30cm across and 20–40cm tall.<ref name=":0" />

== History ==
This species was considered a weed as it would grow on the rice fields of Chinese farmers. This plant was cultivated from a seed by [[George Forrest (botanist)|George Forrest]] in 1908. This species started to gain popularity among commercial growers in England. Within a decade, a new strain which was colourful and fragrant was sold commercially in greenhouses in the USA and throughout Europe.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Mattus|first=Matt|date=2010-02-01|title=A weed by any other name, Primula malacoides|url=https://growingwithplants.com/2010/02/weed-by-any-other-name-primula/|access-date=2020-10-25|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Cultivation ==
This plant can be propagated by seed or by division in late summer.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Primula malacoides|url=https://www.barnhaven.com/asiatic-primula/other-asiatics/primula-malacoides/|access-date=2020-10-25|website=www.barnhaven.com|language=en}}</ref>

This species is a popular ornamental place and can be used as a [[houseplant]] or as a greenhouse plant.<ref name=":0" />

It should be grown in fertile, well-drained soil with regular waterings.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

== Pests and disease ==
This plant is prone to infestation by [[Aphid|aphids]]. Signs of infestation may include: [[Honeydew (secretion)|honeydew]] secretion, [[Gall|galls]], and distortion of leaves.<ref name=":0" />

== Toxicity ==
The leaves may cause irritation. It is advised to wear gloves when handling this plant.<ref name=":0" />

This species may also have [[Allergen|allergenic]] properties with symptoms including rashes and headaches.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" />
